object.question: Why must a response that contains personal data never be stored in a shared cache such as a CDN?
options: A shared cache serves the same stored response to many people
A shared cache deletes stored responses after one hour
A shared cache can only store compressed responses
A shared cache never revalidates its stored copies
object.answer: A shared cache serves the same stored response to many people
object.explanation: Whatever a shared cache stores can be handed to the next person who requests the same URL, so one user's data could reach someone else.
object.sourceQuote: Because a shared cache serves the same stored response to many people, a response that contains personal data must never be stored there.

object.question: What does the s-maxage directive do?
options: It sets a lifetime that overrides max-age, but only for shared caches such as CDNs and proxies
It doubles max-age
It disables caching
It sets a lifetime in minutes
object.answer: It sets a lifetime that overrides max-age, but only for shared caches such as CDNs and proxies
object.explanation: s-maxage is read by shared caches only; the browser keeps using max-age.
object.sourceQuote: Shared caches also understand s-maxage, which overrides max-age for them only.

object.question: What does the s-maxage directive do?
options: It overrides max-age, but only for shared caches
It overrides max-age, but only for the browser
It doubles max-age for every cache on the path
It sets the lifetime in minutes instead of seconds
object.answer: It overrides max-age, but only for shared caches
object.explanation: s-maxage is read by shared caches such as CDNs and proxies; a private cache like the browser keeps using max-age.
object.sourceQuote: Shared caches also understand s-maxage, which overrides max-age for them only.

object.statement: A response sent with no-cache may be stored, but the cache must revalidate it with the server before reusing it.
object.explanation: no-cache does not forbid storing; it requires a check with the server before every reuse. no-store is the directive that forbids keeping the response.
object.sourceQuote: no-cache does not forbid storing a response; it means the cache must revalidate with the server before every reuse.

object.question: A cache revalidates a stale response and the resource has not changed. What does the server send back?
options: 304 Not Modified with no body
200 OK with the full content
404 Not Found with no body
412 Precondition Failed
object.explanation: A 304 tells the cache that its copy is still valid, so nothing is downloaded again.
object.sourceQuote: If nothing changed, the server answers 304 Not Modified without a body.

object.question: A cache revalidates a stale response and the resource has not changed. What does the server send back?
options: 304 Not Modified with no body
200 OK with the full content
404 Not Found with no body
412 Precondition Failed
object.explanation: A 304 tells the cache that its stored copy is still valid, so nothing is downloaded again; a full 200 OK is sent only when the resource changed.
object.sourceQuote: When nothing has changed, the server replies with 304 Not Modified and no body, and the cache marks its copy fresh again.

object.sentence: To revalidate a response that came with an ETag, the cache sends that ETag back in the ____ request header.
object.explanation: If-None-Match carries the ETag; If-Modified-Since is the date-based equivalent used with Last-Modified.
object.sourceQuote: If the stored response included an ETag, an opaque identifier for one version of the resource, the cache sends it back in an If-None-Match header.

object.question: A response is sent with max-age=60, stale-while-revalidate=300. What happens when it is requested three minutes later?
options: It serves the stale copy at once and refreshes it in the background
It answers immediately with the copy it already has stored
It waits for the server to confirm the copy before answering
It discards the copy because its lifetime has fully run out
object.answer: It serves the stale copy at once and refreshes it in the background
object.explanation: After 60 seconds the response is stale, but for the next five minutes it can still be served while the cache refreshes it.
object.sourceQuote: For example, max-age=60, stale-while-revalidate=300 keeps a response fresh for one minute and allows it to be served stale for up to five more minutes while a refresh happens.

issues: The second option is also correct: the cache does answer immediately with the copy it has stored, so two options are defensible.
single_answer.evidence: It answers immediately with the copy it already has stored

issues: Two options describe what happens: serving the stored copy immediately is true under stale-while-revalidate, so the second option cannot be marked wrong.
single_answer.evidence: It answers immediately with the copy it already has stored

object.question: A response is sent with max-age=60, stale-while-revalidate=300. A request for it arrives three minutes later. What does the cache do?
options: Serves the stale copy at once and refreshes it in the background
Serves the copy as fresh without contacting the server at all
Holds the request until the server confirms the copy is valid
Discards the copy and downloads the full response again first
object.answer: Serves the stale copy at once and refreshes it in the background
object.explanation: After one minute the response is stale, but stale-while-revalidate lets the cache serve it for up to five more minutes while it refreshes the copy in the background.
object.sourceQuote: For example, max-age=60, stale-while-revalidate=300 keeps a response fresh for one minute and allows it to be served stale for up to five more minutes while a refresh happens.

object.statement: A file named with a hash of its content can be cached for a year, because any change to the file produces a new URL.
object.explanation: When the content changes, the hash in the name changes too, so pages point to a URL no cache has stored yet.
object.sourceQuote: When the file changes, its name changes, so the HTML points to a URL the cache has never seen.

issues: The statement could be read as saying every hashed file must be cached for a year.
clarity.evidence: can be cached for a year, because every change

object.question: Why should a server list only the headers that really change a response in its Vary header?
object.modelAnswer: Each header named in Vary makes the cache keep a separate copy for every value of that header. Naming headers that do not change the response splits the cache into near-identical copies, so fewer requests find a match and the hit rate drops.
rubric: Vary makes the cache store separate copies per value of the listed headers
Unneeded headers split the cache into more copies than necessary
More copies means fewer requests are served from the cache
object.sourceQuote: Listing too many headers in Vary fragments the cache and lowers the hit rate, so it should name only the headers that actually change the response.
